heading: INT. FUNERAL PARLOUR VIEWING ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FUNERAL PARLOUR VIEWING ROOM - NIGHT
A narrow room of lilac carpet and low lamps.
A closed casket on trestles, a spray of white carnations beside it.
The only sound is the refrigeration unit breathing behind the wall.
AUGUSTINE "GUS" MARLOWE-DIAZ, 50s, in a tidy black suit, sits in the front row with his hat on his knee.
He has the steady manner of a man long used to waiting rooms.
His shoes are polished to a high gloss.
The door opens softly.
DETECTIVE CORDELIA VANTERPOOL, 40s, in a damp mackintosh, enters without a sound.
She stands at the back and does not sit.
Mr. Marlowe-Diaz.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Detective. You came.
units.name: GUS

units.text: You asked me to.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: I did.
units.name: GUS

units.text: She walks the aisle.
Her heels leave faint prints in the nap of the carpet.
She stops beside the casket.
Rests two fingers on its lid, then removes them.
You've kept the lamp low.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: She disliked bright rooms.
units.name: GUS

units.text: So I've heard.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Tea? The undertaker left a flask. It's still warm.
units.name: GUS

units.text: No. Thank you.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: It's good tea.
units.name: GUS

units.text: He pours himself one anyway.
Hands steady.
Offers her the second cup with a small, courteous tilt of the head.
She takes it, finally, and holds it without drinking.
You told the desk sergeant you had something to say about the night she died.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: I did. I do. Only I'd like to say it sitting down, and I'd like you to sit too.
units.name: GUS

units.text: She hesitates, then lowers herself into the chair beside him.
The cup rattles faintly on its saucer.
He notes it, and says nothing.
Forty years, I managed that warehouse. Never late. Never ill.
units.name: GUS

units.text: So the file says.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: And she managed me. In her way.
units.name: GUS

units.text: In her way.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: She kept the accounts. She kept the house. She kept a good many other things besides.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Cordelia turns the cup in its saucer.
The tea has gone still.
Mr. Marlowe-Diaz, the coroner's report mentions bruising on the wrists.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Does it?
units.name: GUS

units.text: It does.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: How unfortunate.
units.name: GUS

units.text: He sips.
Sets the cup down with great care, in exactly the ring it left on the saucer before.
The refrigeration unit cycles off.
The room is suddenly, ferociously quiet.
The nephew told us she had been afraid.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Marcus talks a great deal.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Of whom was she afraid?
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Of the dark, mostly. The dark and the stairs.
units.name: GUS

units.text: The stairs.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Steep. Narrow. I told her a hundred times.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Cordelia sets down her cup.
Reaches into her mackintosh.
Draws out a brown paper evidence bag, and places it on the empty chair on her other side.
You'll want to be careful. That's an old house. Things come apart.
units.name: GUS

units.text: This came apart on a Tuesday.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Tuesday.
units.name: GUS

units.text: You told us you were at the lodge until midnight.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: So I was.
units.name: GUS

units.text: The lodge was closed for repairs. The caretaker has a sign-in book. She signed in alone.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: For the first time, Gus turns his head.
The courteous mask does not slip.
It simply stops being worn.
Cordelia. May I call you Cordelia?
units.name: GUS

units.text: No.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: She did not suffer.
units.name: GUS

units.text: That is not for you to say.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: No. I suppose it isn't.
units.name: GUS

units.text: He rises, brushes his trousers, and settles his hat on his head.
Holds out both wrists, side by side, palms up, as if waiting for a bracelet or a blessing.
Cordelia takes the evidence bag from the chair.
Does not open it.
Does not need to.
Sit down, Mr. Marlowe-Diaz.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: I would rather stand.
units.name: GUS

units.text: Then stand.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Outside, a car door closes.
Footsteps on gravel.
The lamp flickers once, and steadies.
